messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: ECC correctable error spike detected in cluster-prod-eu1 (nodes: gpu-node-12, gpu-node-15, gpu-node-18). Rate 120/min (threshold 30/min). Auto-opened incident thread.

alex: grabbing this. seeing repeated Xid 31 / driver resets and a handful of runtime OOMs leading to container restarts. tagging @priya @sofia.

sofia: with you alex — what's the service impact? any customer pages?

cs_tina: AcmeCorp (prod) reported elevated inference 5xxs ~3m ago; I've opened a customer incident and put them on a short bridge (bridges/INC-7719). They want ETA.

alex: rough sketch: noisy ECC / correctable errors -> NV driver resets (Xid 31) -> some processes lose GPU state -> runtime containers crash/restart -> brief 5xx spikes for multi-tenant models on those nodes. No evidence of data loss.

priya: ok mitigation plan: 1) cordon & drain noisy nodes sequentially, 2) restart nvidia driver / kernel modules if drain doesn't stabilize, 3) failover heavy workloads to spare capacity in us-west while we triage.

sofia: starting drain on gpu-node-12 now.

sofia: ```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=10m
```

alex: logs from gpu-node-12 kernel (excerpt):
```
[ 4213.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Signal: 11 at ip 00007f2b8c1a3b7a
[ 4213.123460] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00 has fallen off the bus.
[ 4213.123470] oom-killer: kill process 27812 (python) score 987 or sacrifice child
[ 4213.123490] containerd: container "runtime-abc" exited with status 137
```

alex: that sequence is consistent: driver reset then kernel OOM + container exit 137 for some large-batch jobs.

deploy-bot: :gear: Canary reroute initiated — redirecting 10% of traffic from eu1 to us-west spare pool to reduce load on affected region.

cs_tina: informing AcmeCorp now: temporary routing and remediation in progress, ETA 20-30 minutes for initial stabilization.

priya: request: SRE team please confirm whether there was any recent kernel/driver rollout to these nodes in the last 24h. I'm seeing older driver version on node metadata.

oncall-logger: recorded: incident-tag=ecc-spike; impacted-nodes=[gpu-node-12,gpu-node-15,gpu-node-18]; customer-bridge=bridges/INC-7719; priority=high.

sofia: drain completed for gpu-node-12, workloads rescheduled. Observed immediate drop in Xid events on that node. Moving to gpu-node-15.

alex: for nodes that still show high Xid rate after drain, plan to reboot and if persists, unload/reload nvidia modules:
```bash
systemctl stop nvidia-persistenced || true
modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia || true
modprobe nvidia || true
```

priya: don't unload modules if production pods are still using devices — ensure cordon+drain first (we already did on 12).

sofia: started drain on gpu-node-15. found one job stuck in CRI OOM loop; we'll evict and restart on spare.

alex: quick telemetry note: disable aggressive preemption for batch jobs? batch jqueues are sending huge single-GPU batches causing higher GPU memory pressure; those jobs amplify driver instability. We should throttle batch size on affected tenants.

cs_tina: AcmeCorp replied: thank you, appreciate the fast action. asked for follow-up RCA and timeline for preventing recurrence.

sofia: gpu-node-15 rebooted after drain+module reload. Xid events decreased by ~80% post-reboot. Observed a couple of residual container OOMs during reschedule.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Traffic reroute at 10% complete; will increment to 25% if stability holds for 10m.

alex: noting a pattern across nodes: ECC correctable errors are non-uniform across GPUs on the same host — could be a thermal/firmware flake. I'll pull SMART/telemetry and ECC counters and open a hardware ticket if it persists.

priya: taking over oncall in 8m. handing off to me if anyone needs escalation. alex — please sync me on the current runbook steps and any immediate follow-ups.

alex: handing off: current state — nodes 12/15 drained+rebooted, 18 still under observation (low Xid rate but intermittent). Canary reroute active. Customer bridge open. Next steps: telemetry dump for nodes, hardware escalation if repeats, tune alerts to reduce noise and auto-evac policy. I'll create follow-up tasks.

priya: thanks — I'll coordinate hardware checks and SRE for driver rollforward plan. cs_tina, will you keep AcmeCorp updated on handoff?

cs_tina: yes, I'll update them and ask for permission to share telemetry logs for RCA.

alex: created follow-ups:
- INC-7719-1: telemetry export and ECC counter analysis
- INC-7719-2: auto-evac sanity check + runbook improvement
- INC-7719-3: customer RCA draft (to be shared after initial triage)

sofia: :thumbsup: good job everyone. I'll keep monitoring node-18 and let you know if Xid rate climbs.

priya: taking lead now. handoff note: priya -> oncall lead; pager cleared for alex. I'll keep this thread updated with remediation progress and will schedule postmortem in 48h.

incident-bot: Incident state change: acknowledged -> mitigated (partial). Tickets created: INC-7719-1, INC-7719-2, INC-7719-3.

priya: final quick note: if anyone sees recurring 31/Xid resets after reboots, DO NOT immediately rejoin to cluster; isolate and preserve kernel logs, and tag hardware for ECC testing.

alex: thanks, handing off.

cs_tina: AcmeCorp updated: they see error rate back to baseline for now, appreciate the update. I'll keep bridge open until final RCA.

sofia: logging off for short break, will watch alerts.

priya: closing loop: postmortem owner assigned to alex, SRE hw checks assigned to sofia, customer comms to cs_tina. I'll follow up with timeline later today. :white_check_mark:
